title: Tools: chat event payload supports tool_use + tool_result content blocks
description: The openclaw web UI's app-tool-stream renders tool calls and results from chat event content blocks: {type:'tool_use', id, name, input} and {type:'tool_result', tool_use_id, content:[{type:'text',text:...}]}. chat events emitted by talon-gateway need to include those blocks so the UI tool stream shows live progress. Per tool call: emit a chat event with state=delta and a content block with type=tool_use as soon as we begin executing; emit a follow-up with type=tool_result once the tool returns. Final assistant message in chat.history should also carry the assembled blocks so refreshes restore the visual.

title: Tools: multi-turn loop in chat.send
description: chat.send currently does a single provider stream then emits state=final. With tools enabled, the loop becomes: stream → on each DeltaToolCall, run the tool via the registry → append tool_result message → re-call provider with the updated history → repeat until the stream terminates with no tool_calls. Cap at MaxToolIterations (default 16) to avoid runaway loops; if the cap is hit emit state=error with errorKind='tool-loop-limit'. ChatStore message shape grows to support tool_use and tool_result content blocks (still text for plain user/assistant turns). Tests with stub provider that emits a tool_call on first stream and text on second confirm the multi-turn cycle, the iteration cap, and the proper history shape feeding back into the second call.

title: Tools: builtin tool registry + read/write/bash/grep/glob impls
description: internal/tools package: Tool interface (Name, Description, ParametersSchema, Run(ctx, input json.RawMessage) (output, error)). Builtins, all workspace-scoped (paths resolved relative to a Workspace string passed at registry construction; absolute paths are rejected unless they resolve under workspace): read (file contents, line range), write (create/overwrite), edit (find/replace by string match), bash (exec a command via /bin/sh -c with timeout, capture stdout+stderr), glob (workspace-relative pattern), grep (regex over files). Each tool has a JSON schema for parameters. Registry exposes ListSpecs() []provider.ToolSpec and Run(ctx, name, input) (output, error). Tests against a temp workspace cover the workspace-confinement guard.
close_reason: internal/tools package landed. Tool interface (Name/Description/ParametersSchema/Run), Registry rooted at a workspace, Specs() returns []provider.ToolSpec ready to attach to a Request. Six builtin tools, all workspace-confined: read (with optional line range), write (creates parent dirs), edit (errors on ambiguous or missing match — echoes Claude Code's edit semantics), bash (CombinedOutput, default 30s/max 5min timeout, exit code in trailer, cwd=workspace), glob (filepath.Glob, workspace-relative results), grep (regex via WalkDir, max 200 matches, skips .git/node_modules/.talon, supports include glob filter). resolveInWorkspace uses filepath.Rel to reject path traversal and lookalike-prefix attacks (workspace=/foo, target=/foobar/x is rejected). 23 tests cover the registry surface, every tool's happy path, traversal rejection, ambiguous-match error, exit code formatting, and context cancellation tolerance.

title: Tools: provider interface tool support + OpenAI tool-call streaming
description: Add tool support to provider.Provider: (1) Request.Tools []ToolSpec advertising available tools to the model, (2) new Delta variant DeltaToolCall carrying {id, name, argsJSON} once a call's args have fully arrived. OpenAI impl: serialize tools into the request body shape (tools:[{type:'function',function:{name,description,parameters}}]), parse the streamed delta.tool_calls[].function.{name,arguments} fragments by index, accumulate args as JSON-stringified fragments per index, and emit one DeltaToolCall per completed call when finish_reason becomes 'tool_calls' or the stream ends. ToolSpec is a small struct {Name, Description, ParametersSchema json.RawMessage} so callers can pass any JSON-schema. Tests with httptest server using a recorded SSE transcript for tool-calls. Out of scope: actual tool execution; multi-turn loop.
close_reason: Provider interface gained tool support: Request.Tools []ToolSpec ({Name, Description, ParametersSchema}), DeltaToolCall variant carrying *ToolCall ({ID, Name, ArgumentsJSON}), Message extended with ToolCalls []ToolCall (assistant turn invoking tools) and ToolCallID string (role=tool result turns). RoleTool added. OpenAI provider serializes tools as tools:[{type:'function',function:{name,description,parameters}}], assistant tool_calls as tool_calls:[{id,type:function,function:{name,arguments}}], tool results as {role:tool,tool_call_id,content}. SSE pump accumulates per-index tool_call fragments (id+name on first chunk, args fragments thereafter) and flushes one DeltaToolCall per index when finish_reason='tool_calls' or stream ends. Tests: tool-call accumulation across 3 args fragments → single assembled call, request body includes tools field when set, tools omitted when absent, assistant tool_calls + tool result messages serialize correctly.

title: Native agent.identity.get on talon-gateway
description: The web UI calls agent.identity.get {agentId} to render the assistant's name + avatar in the chat header. Without it, every assistant message says 'Assistant' instead of the IDENTITY.md-derived name (e.g. 'Clawdia 🦞'). Implementation: resolve the agent's workspace from merged config (per-agent workspace field, fallback to agents.defaults.workspace), read <workspace>/IDENTITY.md, parse the markdown bullet list ('- **Name:** X', '- **Emoji:** Y', '- **Avatar:** Z'), return {agentId, name, emoji, avatar}. avatar may be a workspace-relative path, http(s) URL, or data URI. Missing IDENTITY.md returns null (UI tolerates null) so the chat header falls back to agent id.
close_reason: Native agent.identity.get on talon-gateway. Resolves agent's workspace from per-agent .workspace field with fallback to agents.defaults.workspace, then reads <workspace>/IDENTITY.md and parses the markdown bullet list ('- **Name:** X', '- **Emoji:** Y', '- **Avatar:** Z'). Returns {agentId, name, emoji, avatar} where avatar falls back to emoji when the field is empty (matches openclaw behavior). Unknown agents and missing IDENTITY.md return nil so the UI's null-tolerant path falls back to the agent id. Parser is tolerant of whitespace + key case, ignores italics-wrapped continuation hints like '_(workspace-relative path...)_'. Tests cover the real openclaw template format, filled-avatar shorthand, empty document, case/whitespace tolerance, defaults workspace fallback, unknown agent, missing IDENTITY.md, and missing agentId param.

title: talon-gateway: print UI deep-link on startup, add talon ui open
description: The gateway URL (ws://localhost:18790) is the single most-typed string in dev — and forgettable after a browser cache clear. Two improvements: (1) on 'talon gateway run' startup log a click-through URL like 'http://localhost:5173/chat#gatewayUrl=ws%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A18790' (token included when --auth=token) so the user can copy/paste from the terminal. UI host defaults to http://localhost:5173 (vite dev) but is overridable with --ui-host. (2) New 'talon ui open' command that prints the URL and (on darwin) launches it via 'open'. Also 'talon ui url' for scriptable use. No-op when stdout isn't a TTY for the auto-open; print only.
close_reason: Two pieces shipped: (1) 'talon gateway run' now logs a click-through UI URL on startup, e.g. 'UI:  http://localhost:5173/chat?session=main#gatewayUrl=ws%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A18790' (with &token=... when --auth=token). UI host defaults to http://localhost:5173 (vite dev). (2) New 'talon ui' parent with two subcommands: 'talon ui url' prints the deep-link, 'talon ui open' prints AND launches the system browser via 'open' (darwin), 'xdg-open' (linux), or 'rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler' (windows). Flags: --ui-host, --gateway-host, --gateway-port, --token, --session, --path. Token/gatewayUrl land in the fragment so they don't appear in HTTP request logs. Tests cover defaults, token+session combo, empty-session = no query, custom path.

title: Native chat.send + chat event stream (uses provider interface)
description: Implement chat.send and the chat event stream on talon-gateway. chat.send accepts {sessionKey, message, idempotencyKey} (matching openclaw shape) and: (1) resolves sessionKey to an agentId (default sessionKey form is agent:<agentId>:<agentId>), (2) loads that agent's primary model from merged config, (3) creates a Provider for the model's provider name (factory lookup), (4) launches a streaming completion in a goroutine, (5) fans Provider Deltas out to the originating session as 'chat' events with the openclaw event shape: {runId, sessionKey, seq, state:'streaming'|'final'|'aborted'|'error', message:{phase:'assistant',role:'assistant',content:[{type:'text',text:...}]}, errorKind?, errorMessage?}. Idempotency: if a runId is already active for {sessionKey, idempotencyKey} return the existing runId and replay events from a per-session ring buffer (cap 100 events) for late subscribers. Acceptance: openclaw web UI at http://localhost:5173/chat?session=main can send a message and watch tokens stream in when pointed at talon-gateway with the OpenAI provider configured. Depends on talon-ax2 (interface), talon-e21 (OpenAI impl).
close_reason: chat.send + chat event stream landed on talon-gateway. ChatHandler in internal/server/chat.go: parses sessionKey via AgentIDFromSessionKey('agent:<id>:<convo>' → '<id>'), resolves agent's primary model via AgentResolver, materializes provider via ProviderFactory, appends user msg to ChatStore (in-memory), then spawns a streaming goroutine that fans provider.Delta events out as openclaw-shaped 'chat' events (state: streaming|final|error; payload includes runId, sessionKey, seq, message.content[0].text). Idempotency: same {sessionKey, idempotencyKey} returns the existing runId. Session.PushEvent is now write-mutex serialized. cmd/talon/gateway_chat.go provides the concrete configAgentResolver (reads agents.list[].model.primary from merged config) and agentProviderFactory (loads openai:default api_key from <openclaw>/agents/<agentId>/agent/auth-profiles.json; only 'openai' is implemented). gateway run wires both into server.Config and logs 'chat=enabled, providers=openai'. Tests cover param validation, agent-not-found, provider-unavailable, missing provider segment, idempotency same-runId, distinct runIds without idempotency key, sessionKey parsing edge cases, ChatStore append+snapshot+isolation. Out of scope: ring-buffer replay for late subscribers, multi-provider, fallbacks, system prompts, tool use.

title: Native models.list RPC handler on talon-gateway
description: Wire the models.list registry handler in internal/server. Reads model definitions from talon's merged config (models.providers.<provider>.models[]) and returns the same envelope shape the openclaw gateway emits today: {models:[{id,name,provider,contextWindow,input:[modalities],reasoning,alias?},...]}. Independent of provider work — just a config read.
close_reason: Native agents.list, models.list, and config.schema landed on talon-gateway via internal/server/reads.go (ReadHandler). agents.list synthesizes the openclaw envelope shape (agents:[{id, model:{primary,fallbacks}, workspace?, name?}], defaultId, mainKey, scope) — primary resolves with the same three-tier precedence as configAgentResolver (per-agent .model.primary → per-agent .model string → agents.defaults.model.primary), and fallbacks come from defaults.model.fallbacks. defaultId prefers 'main' or falls back to the first agent. models.list flattens models.providers.<name>.models[] and decorates each row with the alias from agents.defaults.models[<key>].alias when present; sorted by id for stable output. config.schema returns the cached envelope at ~/.talon/cache/config-schema.json verbatim, with a helpful error message pointing at 'talon config schema --refresh' when the cache is missing or invalid. Wired into gateway run via server.Config.Paths. Session.PushEvent is now nil-safe (returns errNoSession instead of panicking) so chat tests with stub Sessions don't crash from background goroutines. Tests cover model precedence, defaultId fallback, alias decoration, sort order, missing/invalid schema cache, and registry registration.

title: Native agents.list + config.schema RPC handlers on talon-gateway
description: Wire two registry handlers in internal/server: agents.list reads talon's merged config and returns {agents:[{id,name,model:{primary,fallbacks},workspace}], defaultId, mainKey, scope}. config.schema reads the cached schema envelope at ~/.talon/cache/config-schema.json and returns it (or returns a structured error if the cache is empty so the UI knows to refresh). Both handlers read-only; no mutation. Acceptance: openclaw web UI's agent picker shows the configured agents when pointed at talon-gateway; config screens render. Tests against a fixture config. Independent of provider work; can ship in parallel with talon-ax2.
close_reason: Native agents.list, models.list, and config.schema landed on talon-gateway via internal/server/reads.go (ReadHandler). agents.list synthesizes the openclaw envelope shape (agents:[{id, model:{primary,fallbacks}, workspace?, name?}], defaultId, mainKey, scope) — primary resolves with the same three-tier precedence as configAgentResolver (per-agent .model.primary → per-agent .model string → agents.defaults.model.primary), and fallbacks come from defaults.model.fallbacks. defaultId prefers 'main' or falls back to the first agent. models.list flattens models.providers.<name>.models[] and decorates each row with the alias from agents.defaults.models[<key>].alias when present; sorted by id for stable output. config.schema returns the cached envelope at ~/.talon/cache/config-schema.json verbatim, with a helpful error message pointing at 'talon config schema --refresh' when the cache is missing or invalid. Wired into gateway run via server.Config.Paths. Session.PushEvent is now nil-safe (returns errNoSession instead of panicking) so chat tests with stub Sessions don't crash from background goroutines. Tests cover model precedence, defaultId fallback, alias decoration, sort order, missing/invalid schema cache, and registry registration.

title: OpenAI provider implementation (streaming chat completions)
description: Concrete Provider implementation for OpenAI in internal/provider/openai. Reads the api_key from <openclaw>/agents/<agentId>/agent/auth-profiles.json under 'openai:default'. Calls https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions with stream=true; parses SSE; emits TextDelta per token chunk and FinalUsage on the [DONE] terminator. No tool-use, no function-calling, no JSON mode. Acceptance: integration test with a stub HTTP server that emits a recorded SSE transcript; provider produces the expected Delta sequence. Out of scope: rate-limit handling beyond surfacing errors. Depends on talon-ax2 (provider interface).
notes: The Anthropic OAuth profile in this project flows through Claude Code; that is intentionally NOT implemented in this issue — it is materially harder and tracked separately.
close_reason: OpenAI provider implementation in internal/provider/openai. Provider.Stream POSTs to /chat/completions with stream=true and stream_options.include_usage=true; SSE pump translates each data: chunk into a TextDelta and emits a final UsageDelta when the API reports it. Auth is plumbed via LoadAPIKey(authProfilesPath, profileID) which reads openclaw's auth-profiles.json and returns the openai:default api_key. Setup errors (missing key, non-openai provider segment, HTTP non-200) come back via the error return; mid-stream parse errors arrive as DeltaError followed by channel close. Tests with httptest server cover happy path (recorded SSE transcript: 'Hello, world' + 12/3 token usage), HTTP 401 surfacing, missing-key rejection, wrong-provider rejection, malformed-chunk → error delta. LoadAPIKey tests cover happy path, wrong-provider mismatch, oauth-type rejection, missing-profile error.

title: Provider interface (internal/provider package)
description: Design and ship the streaming-completion provider interface that talon-gateway's chat.send will use. Types only in this issue — no concrete provider impl. Goals: (1) define internal/provider/provider.go with a Provider interface that takes a streaming Request and returns a stream of Delta events; (2) Request shape: ModelID (the openclaw 'provider/model' form, e.g. openai/gpt-5.4-mini), Messages ([]Message with Role+Content), System string, Temperature/MaxTokens/etc as a generic Options; (3) Delta shape covers TextDelta, ReasoningDelta, FinalUsage (input/output tokens), and ErrorDelta; (4) Provider.Stream(ctx, req) returns (<-chan Delta, error). The provider implementation receives auth credentials separately (probably via a Credentials interface or a field on the provider struct returned by a Factory). Out of scope: actual HTTP/SDK calls, model catalogs, tool-use, multi-modal. Acceptance: types compile, interface is documented, a unit test exercises a stub provider that emits a fixed delta sequence to confirm channel semantics. Blocks talon-aws sub-work for chat.send (talon-aws-5) and OpenAI impl (talon-aws-2).
notes: User direction (2026-04-27): build the provider interface up-front, not bolted on after a hardcoded first-cut. Anthropic goes through Claude Code OAuth (claude-cli) so it is the *harder* provider; OpenAI is the simpler first concrete impl since it has a normal API key in auth-profiles.json.
close_reason: internal/provider package landed: Provider interface (Name() + Stream(ctx, Request) (<-chan Delta, error)), Request/Message/Options/ModelID types with Provider()/Model() helpers, Delta with DeltaKind discriminant (Text/Reasoning/Usage/Error) plus Usage. Stub provider for tests replays a recorded script, records calls, honors ctx cancel, terminates on DeltaError. Tests: ModelID split, in-order replay, channel close after error delta, prompt close on ctx cancel. Compile-time assertion that Stub satisfies Provider. Credentials are NOT in the interface — concrete providers handle their own auth (per design).

title: Gateway WS connect handshake (login)
description: Implement the openclaw-compatible WS connect handshake on claw-gateway so the control UI can log in. Spec (from openclaw client-kQ1-TM3I.js): server emits connect.challenge event with {nonce, ts} on connect. Client sends req method=connect with ConnectParamsSchema (minProtocol, maxProtocol, client.{id,version,platform,mode}, optional auth.{token,password,deviceToken,bootstrapToken}, role, scopes). Server replies with res payload shaped as hello-ok: {protocol, server.{version,connId}, features.{methods[], events[]}, snapshot.{presence[], health, stateVersion, uptimeMs, authMode?}, policy.{maxPayload, maxBufferedBytes, tickIntervalMs}, optional auth.{role, scopes[], issuedAtMs}}. Auth modes: none/token (skip password/trusted-proxy for now). Reject pre-connect frames except 'connect'. After connect, dispatch req frames to a registry; unknown methods return ErrorCodes shape.
acceptance_criteria: control UI can complete login against claw gateway; existing claw client connects without changes; unknown RPC methods return a structured error.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bootstrap gateway scaffolding (Go backend + React/TS/Vite frontend)
description: Scaffolding only, no business logic. Go binary at cmd/claw-gateway with WS handler stub + healthz. React/TS/Vite SPA at web/. Wire Makefile targets for both. This unblocks all subsequent gateway server work tracked under claw-aws.
close_reason: Closed

title: BUG: wrong RPC method name 'health.get'
description: claw calls 'health.get' but the openclaw gateway registers the method as 'health' (no .get suffix). Confirmed by reading /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/gateway-cli-ToC6xhTV.js:1142,1192 — both call callGatewayCli('health'). claw's healthCmd in cmd/claw/main.go:94 must use 'health'. Likely means current 'claw health' fails against a real gateway. Audit other claw RPC calls (config.schema, models.list, agents.list) — those names DO appear in openclaw's source as registered methods, so they're fine.
close_reason: Closed

title: Upstream: bonjour bundled JS out of sync with TS source
description: openclaw dist/extensions/bonjour/index.js registers/unregisters its unhandled-rejection handler per cycle. When @homebridge/ciao rejects with CIAO ANNOUNCEMENT/PROBING CANCELLED during svc.destroy(), the handler is gone before the reject fires unhandled. Host installUnhandledRejectionHandler then calls process.exit(1). TS source already has the correct lifecycle (handler at top-level start/stop). Just needs a rebuild + release. Workaround applied: plugins.entries.bonjour.enabled=false.

title: Gateway server in Go (option A)
description: WS server with the same frame format and auth. Start with read-only methods: commands.list, health.get, config.get, models.list, agents.list. Multi-session. This is the multi-week chunk.

title: talon config schema --section <name>
description: openclaw config schema supports section filtering. Inspect config.schema RPC params and pass through.
close_reason: Added --section flag to 'talon config schema' that filters the cached/freshly-fetched envelope to a named subschema. Supports nested dotted paths (gateway.auth → schema.properties.gateway.properties.auth). 5 unit tests for ExtractSchemaSection covering top-level, nested, empty, missing, and invalid-segment cases. Smoke-tested against the live cached schema.

title: talon config set whitespace minimization
description: tidwall/sjson + pretty re-formats the entire file, producing noisy git diffs. Either (a) use a writer that only re-pretties the changed subtree, or (b) match openclaw's exact 2-space indent and key order. Investigate ~1h, fix ~1-3h.
close_reason: Investigation found the format is already byte-identical to openclaw's JSON.stringify(v, null, 2) + '\n'. Real noise source was idempotent sets — same value still rotated .bak files and appended audit lines. Fix: short-circuit Set/Unset when post-pretty bytes equal on-disk bytes (no rotation, no audit, no write). CLI prints 'set X — no change (value already matches; overlay file untouched)'. Tests: TestSet_IdempotentSetIsNoOp, TestSet_WriteFormatMatchesOpenclaw (locks the openclaw byte-compat), TestUnset_IdempotentWhenAlreadyDeleted. Smoke-tested: redundant set produces no .bak.1 rotation.

title: Pretty/columnar output for typed commands
description: claw models, claw agents list, etc. dump raw JSON. Match openclaw's tabular output: id, modality, ctx, reasoning, configured. ~1 session.
close_reason: talon models and talon agents list now render tab-aligned tables by default; --json keeps the raw RPC payload. Models columns: ID, MODALITIES, CTX (compacted to K/M, including 131072→128K rounding), REASONING, ALIAS, NAME. Agents columns: ID (default flagged), MODEL (primary), WORKSPACE (~-shortened), FALLBACKS (count), NAME. emit() no longer hardcodes 'flagJSON || true'. Tests in cmd/talon/render_test.go cover empty payloads, ordering, ctx formatting, and column presence.

title: Reuse single WS connection for sequential RPCs
description: Today every 'claw call X' opens a fresh WS, does the connect-challenge handshake, and tears it down. For one-shot CLI that's fine, but a REPL/interactive mode benefits from connection reuse. Add a daemonless 'session' or socket the CLI hands off to.

title: Tools: DeepSeek provider (OpenAI-compatible)
description: DeepSeek's API is OpenAI-compatible (openai-completions). New internal/provider/deepseek that mostly delegates to the openai package, just with a different baseURL (https://api.deepseek.com) and api_key profile (deepseek:default). agentProviderFactory grows a 'deepseek' case that loads the deepseek:default key from auth-profiles.json and constructs the provider. Tool calling shape is identical to OpenAI's so this should be a small wrapper.

title: Tools: sandbox confinement + approval RPC
description: Production-grade execution gating. Today bash + write are workspace-scoped via path resolution; we need: (1) a per-tool risk classifier (read/glob/grep=safe; write/edit=needs-confirm; bash=needs-confirm with command sniffing for rm/sudo/curl); (2) gateway emits exec-approval-request event with {requestId, tool, input, classification} and waits on a synchronous approval reply RPC; UI prompts the user; (3) policy file at ~/.talon/exec-policy.json with allow/deny patterns to bypass the prompt for known-safe operations. MVP: just the classifier + a 'block list' for outside-workspace paths and clearly destructive bash patterns; the approval round-trip can land later.

title: Native chat.history (in-memory)
description: Implement chat.history on talon-gateway. Records each {sessionKey -> []Message} in an in-memory map (sync.Mutex-guarded). chat.send appends both the user message (when received) and the assistant message (when state=final) to the store. chat.history returns the last N messages for the requested sessionKey (param 'limit', default 50). No persistence yet — server restart loses history. Depends on talon-aws-5 (chat.send) since the store is shared.
close_reason: chat.history landed. ChatHandler.handleHistory returns {messages:[{__openclaw:{id,seq}, role, content:[{type:text,text}], timestamp}]} matching openclaw's shape (subset). Limit param caps the tail (limit<=0 means unlimited). Unknown sessionKey returns empty messages array (not an error). Stable per-message id derived from FNV-1a(sessionKey)^index so React keys don't churn across reads. Tests cover stored-message round-trip + id stability + uniqueness, limit truncation, unknown-session empty, missing-sessionKey rejection, both methods registered.

title: Config-change policy: never auto-restart, never auto-load; HUP-reload where possible
description:
Policy decision (2026-04-27): config writes by talon must never trigger a gateway restart or auto-reload. The user explicitly opted out of file-watcher-based reloads. Where supported, a config field should be hot-reloadable via SIGHUP to the running gateway. Where not, talon's 'config set' output should tell the user a restart is needed.

Scope:
1. Path-class registry — for each known config dot-path, classify as (a) hot-reloadable on SIGHUP, (b) effective-on-next-RPC (no signal needed), (c) requires restart. Initial pass: gateway.* probably (c); channels.* probably (a); models.* probably (b); auth.profiles probably (b); plugins.entries.<x>.enabled requires restart; agents.list probably (a) for non-workspace fields.
2. cmd/talon/config set output — replace the bare 'set <path>' message with a class-aware hint:
   - (a): 'set <path>. Send SIGHUP to the running gateway to apply (or restart).'
   - (b): 'set <path>. Will be picked up on the next RPC.'
   - (c): 'set <path>. Restart the gateway to apply.'
3. Confirm openclaw's gateway actually handles SIGHUP. Today openclaw probably just re-reads on next request; SIGHUP plumbing may not exist. If so, this issue depends on adding SIGHUP support to talon's embedded gateway and/or filing an openclaw upstream issue for the same.
4. The opposite policy — talon must NEVER spawn a file watcher on ~/.openclaw or ~/.talon to auto-detect config changes. Reload is always explicit (signal or restart).
5. Document in CLAUDE.md / docs/architecture.md.

Note: openclaw's existing 'config set' output ends with 'Restart the gateway to apply' regardless of path. We are intentionally diverging from that — talon classifies per-path. PARITY.md should call this out as an intentional difference, not a parity gap.
close_reason: Phase 1 landed: internal/config/reload.go with ReloadClass enum (next-rpc/hup/restart), ClassifyReload registry, ParseReloadClass and Hint. cmd/talon config set emits class-aware hints after writes; --reload override accepts next-rpc|hup|restart for unknown paths. Restart-class entries: gateway.port/bind/auth.*, gateway.tailscale.*, gateway.controlUi.*, plugins.entries.*.enabled, plugins.deny, plugins.load.paths, skills.*. HUP class empty pending talon-gateway SIGHUP handler (Phase 2: talon-f06). Tests cover all listed paths + override parsing + Hint shapes. PARITY.md documents the intentional divergence from openclaw's 'restart to apply' universal message. CLAUDE.md updated with explicit-reload policy + registry pointers.

title: Upstream: openclaw config.schema RPC emits dangling $defs refs
description:
The schema returned by the openclaw config.schema RPC contains $ref pointers to #/$defs/<name> (secretInput, secretRef, account, audioFormatPolicy, route, stt, ...) but does not include a top-level $defs block. Instead, those definitions appear inline inside specific properties (e.g. plugins.entries.feishu.config.secretInput).

Effect on talon: schema compilation via santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 fails with 'json-pointer in ... #/$defs/X not found'. talon's 'config validate' falls back to syntax-only and warns; 'config validate --strict' surfaces the compile error. See ErrSchemaCompileFailed in internal/config/schema.go.

Fix should land upstream in openclaw (the schema generator should either emit a top-level $defs block or rewrite the refs to point at the inline locations). Once fixed, talon will get full schema-aware validation automatically — no talon code change needed.

Reproduce: talon gateway call config.schema | grep -E '"$ref":' | head; jq 'keys[] | select(. == "$defs")' returns nothing.

title: Secrets: macOS Keychain backend, no plaintext in files/env by default
description:
Policy: talon must not store secret values in ~/.talon/openclaw.json or environment variables by default. Replacements should reference a keychain-backed provider.

Current state:
- ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json holds plaintext secrets (gateway.auth.token, channels.telegram.botToken, plugins.entries.brave.config.webSearch.apiKey, skills.entries.openai-whisper-api.apiKey).
- The existing ~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw-gateway-with-1password shim already uses 'security find-generic-password' to fetch a 1Password service-account token from the macOS Keychain, then exports it as OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN. So Keychain is already on the bootstrap path for 1P users.

Scope:
1. Define a talon-side SecretStore interface (Get/Set/Delete by service+account+key).
2. Implement a macOS Keychain backend (Go: prefer github.com/zalando/go-keyring for cross-platform abstraction, fall back to /usr/bin/security CLI shell-out if cgo is undesirable). Linux (libsecret) and Windows (Credential Manager) are bonus targets.
3. Decide the on-disk shape: when 'talon config set' targets a known-secret path, write a SecretRef pointer into ~/.talon/openclaw.json instead of the literal value. Shape options:
   (a) Reuse openclaw's SecretRef ({source, provider, id}) and add a 'keychain' source — requires openclaw runtime support to resolve.
   (b) Introduce a 'talon-secret://service/account' URI form — talon-only, openclaw won't resolve it.
   (c) Bridge: talon writes an 'exec'-source SecretRef pointing at a 'talon secret-resolve' subcommand that reads from Keychain. Works with openclaw today via the existing exec provider.
4. Detect known-secret paths (registry of paths considered sensitive: gateway.auth.token, gateway.auth.password, channels.*.{botToken,token}, plugins.entries.*.config.*.apiKey, skills.entries.*.apiKey, etc.).
5. CLI surface: 'talon config set --keychain' (force keychain backend), 'talon config set' on a known-secret path (default keychain), 'talon secrets list/get/set/delete' for direct management.
6. Migration helper: 'talon secrets migrate' scans ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json for plaintext secrets and offers to move them into Keychain + write talon-overlay refs.

Open questions:
- Native 1Password (op CLI shell-out, or 1P Connect HTTP API, or 1P SDK) vs extending the existing shim. Native gives non-Mac portability and avoids the bootstrap-token-in-Keychain step, but pulls in a heavier dep. Decide before implementation; may end up shipping both modes.
- Coordination with openclaw: option (a) above needs upstream changes; option (c) works today but adds an exec hop.
- Test strategy: keychain access prompts the user. Need a fake-store backend for unit tests, plus an integration-test harness that uses a sandbox keychain (security create-keychain).

Depends on talon-ekv landing first (SecretRef shape parity) so we have the data types to point at.

title: talon-gateway: SIGHUP handler that re-reads merged config (Phase 2 of talon-5zx)
description:
Phase 1 of talon-5zx shipped the path-class registry and CLI hints. Phase 2: make talon's embedded gateway server (internal/server/) actually honor SIGHUP by re-reading the layered config and applying changes for paths classified as ReloadHUP.

Scope:
1. Wire signal.Notify(SIGHUP) in cmd/talon/gateway.go's gatewayRunCmd alongside SIGINT/SIGTERM (today only the latter trigger shutdown).
2. On SIGHUP, call into a new server.Server.Reload(ctx, newCfg) that swaps in a new config snapshot. Concurrent RPC handlers must observe the new value on their next access (atomic.Pointer[Config] or sync.Mutex around a *Config field).
3. Decide what's actually reloadable: this PR only commits to the talon embedded-gateway side. internal/server today only serves 'health' so the reloadable surface is small; once more handlers land, more paths can move from ReloadNextRPC to ReloadHUP in internal/config/reload.go.
4. Cannot reload: listener address (port/bind), TLS material, plugin loader state — those stay ReloadRestart.
5. Tests: signal an in-process *server.Server with a fake SIGHUP-equivalent (exposed Reload method called directly), verify config swap, no goroutine leaks.
6. Docs: docs/architecture.md gains a 'Reload semantics' section under 'Embedded gateway'.

Also covers the upstream openclaw side: talon's CLI hints recommend SIGHUP for hup-class paths, but if openclaw's gateway doesn't handle SIGHUP, the user's signal is a no-op. File a separate openclaw issue if confirming that. For now, talon's hints are honest — 'send SIGHUP (or restart)' covers both cases.

value: Project priority (2026-04-27): the user explicitly values that talon is 'so much faster than openclaw'. Speed/latency is a load-bearing differentiator — preserve it when making architectural decisions (favor persistent connections, in-process state, avoiding extra hops; be skeptical of features that add latency even when they look 'cleaner').

Provider integration (2026-04-27): Anthropic in this project goes through Claude Code's OAuth (claude-cli profile), NOT the raw Anthropic API — that makes it the harder provider, not the easier one. First concrete provider should be OpenAI (api_key in ~/.openclaw/agents/<agent>/agent/auth-profiles.json under 'openai:default'). The provider interface is load-bearing and must be designed up-front, not bolted onto a hardcoded first-cut. Order: provider abstraction → OpenAI implementation → chat.send wired through the interface.
Push policy (2026-04-27): direct push to main is OK until the project reaches a 'usable point'. No feature branches / PRs required for now. Revisit when the gateway server can stand on its own.

Roadmap (2026-04-27): after current config-polish work (talon-7vk whitespace, talon-8eb pretty output), priority is agent/chat surface (talon-dcj chat→TUI, talon-z8h thinking deltas, talon-xhg extractAssistantText, talon-c0b sessions), then tools and plugins. Order: config polish → agents/chat → tools/plugins.
